# language: de
@sample @localised
Funktionalität: Lokalisierte Gherkin-Schlüsselwörter
  Deutsche Schlüsselwörter. Der Report muss `keywordType` (Context/Action/Outcome) für das
  Styling verwenden und das rohe Schlüsselwort anzeigen — siehe SPEC 4.3. Jeder Code der
  auf "Given"/"When"/"Then" vergleicht, scheitert hier.

  Grundlage:
    Angenommen der Katalog ist befüllt

  Szenario: Ein Produkt in den Warenkorb legen
    Angenommen ein Produkt "Widget" kostet 9.99
    Wenn ich es in den Warenkorb lege
    Dann sollte die Summe 9.99 betragen

  Szenariogrundriss: Rabattstufen
    Angenommen ein Produkt "<name>" kostet <preis>
    Wenn ich die Rabattstufe "<stufe>" anwende
    Dann sollte die Summe <erwartet> betragen

    Beispiele:
      | name   | preis | stufe | erwartet |
      | Widget | 100   | keine | 100      |
      | Widget | 100   | zehn  | 90       |

@sample @hooks
Feature: Failing hooks
  The highest-traffic CI failure mode (SPEC 4.3): a scenario whose Before hook throws has
  a failed outcome but ZERO failed steps. Without hook rows in the timeline the report
  would show "everything skipped" and no error anywhere.

  @fail-before-hook
  Scenario: Before hook throws
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then the basket total should be 9.99

  @fail-after-hook
  Scenario: After hook throws though every step passed
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then the basket total should be 9.99

Feature: Attachments and evidence
  Produces the attachment envelopes the report's evidence renderers dispatch on (SPEC 3.2):
  an image, a SpecReport HTTP-exchange JSON payload, a plain JSON file with no discriminator
  (must degrade to a plain JSON view), text output, and the run-meta payload.

  @ui
  Scenario: A step that attaches a screenshot
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then I attach a screenshot
    And the basket total should be 9.99

  @ui @known-fail
  Scenario: A failing step that attaches a screenshot
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then I attach a screenshot
    And the basket total should be 404.00

  @api
  Scenario: A step that records an HTTP exchange
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    And I add it to the basket

  @api @known-fail

  @api
  Scenario: A step with several HTTP exchanges

    And I add it to the basket
    When I record 3 HTTP exchanges
    Then the basket total should be 9.99

    Then the basket total should be 9.99

@sample @basics
Feature: Basics
  Covers the ordinary shapes: passing scenario, failing scenario, skipped-after-failure,
  tags, data tables and doc strings.

  Background:
    Given the catalogue is seeded
    And the session is anonymous

  @smoke
  Scenario: A wholly passing scenario
    Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then the basket total should be 9.99

  @smoke @known-fail
  Scenario: A failing assertion, with steps skipped after it
    Given a product "Gadget" priced 19.99
    When I add it to the basket
    Then the basket total should be 999.00
    And the basket should contain 1 item
    And the checkout button should be enabled

  Scenario: A data table step
    Given the following products
      | Name    | Price | Stock |
      | Widget  | 9.99  | 12    |
      | Gadget  | 19.99 | 0     |
      | Doohick | 4.50  | 7     |
    When I add all in-stock products to the basket
    Then the basket total should be 14.49

  Scenario: A doc string step
    Given the following order note
      """
      Please gift-wrap this order.
      Leave with the neighbour at number 12 if we are out.
      """
    When I submit the order note
    Then the order note should be 2 lines long

  @pending-work
  Scenario: A pending step
    Given a product "Prototype" priced 0.01
    When the pricing engine is rewritten
    Then the basket total should be 0.01

  @undefined-step
  Scenario: An undefined step
    Given a product "Mystery" priced 1.00
    When I do something nobody has implemented yet
    Then the basket total should be 1.00

@sample @outlines
Feature: Scenario Outlines
  Exercises Examples tables, including a deliberate duplicate row so the parser's
  example-row-index tiebreaker in scenario identity (SPEC 6.2) is provable.

  Scenario Outline: Discount bands
    Given a product "<name>" priced <price>
    When I apply the "<band>" discount band
    Then the basket total should be <expected>

    Examples: Standard bands
      | name    | price | band     | expected |
      | Widget  | 100   | none     | 100      |
      | Widget  | 100   | ten      | 90       |
      | Gadget  | 50    | half     | 25       |

    Examples: Duplicate rows on purpose
      | name    | price | band     | expected |
      | Doohick | 20    | ten      | 18       |
      | Doohick | 20    | ten      | 18       |

  Scenario Outline: An outline row that fails
    Given a product "<name>" priced <price>
    When I apply the "<band>" discount band
    Then the basket total should be <expected>

    Examples:
      | name   | price | band | expected |
      | Widget | 100   | ten  | 90       |
      | Widget | 100   | ten  | 12345    |

@sample @rules
Feature: Rules and grouping
  Gherkin `Rule:` blocks. The report must group Feature -> Rule -> Scenario (SPEC 4.2);
  without a Rule slot these four scenarios would merge into one flat list.

  Rule: In-stock products can be bought

    Background:
      Given the catalogue is seeded

    Example: Buying an in-stock product succeeds
      Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
      When I add it to the basket
      Then the basket total should be 9.99

    Example: Buying two in-stock products sums the total
      Given a product "Widget" priced 9.99
      And a product "Doohick" priced 4.50
      When I add all in-stock products to the basket
      Then the basket total should be 14.49

  Rule: Out-of-stock products cannot be bought

    Example: Adding an out-of-stock product is rejected
      Given a product "Gadget" priced 19.99 with no stock
      When I add it to the basket
      Then the basket should contain 0 items

    Example: An out-of-stock rejection that fails on purpose
      Given a product "Gadget" priced 19.99 with no stock
      When I add it to the basket
      Then the basket should contain 1 item
